* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and
lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...

River LA from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to

Coastal waters from the Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana out 20 NM...

At 926 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of showers, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts. This
cluster of showers is generally located along a line extending from
12 nm northeast of Eugene Island 189 to 13 nm northeast of Louisiana
Offshore Oil Port. The cluster of showers was nearly stationary.

Mariners can expect widespread gusty winds to around 30 knots and
higher waves. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this
activity passes.

Brief, weak waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on
alert in case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

NWSheadline: A CLUSTER OF SHOWERS OVER THE WATERS

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Waters from Boothville LA to Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River out 20 nm; Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 5 at 9:24AM CDT until October 5 at 10:30AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Boothville LA to Southwest Pass of the
Mississippi River out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20
NM...

* Until 1030 AM CDT.

* At 924 AM CDT, a shower capable of producing waterspouts was
located 17 nm northeast of Pilottown. The shower was nearly
stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels and oil rigs...and create suddenly higher waves.
Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The shower will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Strong winds will be dangerous for boaters or anyone near the water.
Boaters should avoid waterspouts and never try to navigate near them.
Make sure all on board are wearing life jackets. Seek shelter or move
to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

hydration.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and

properties.areaDesc: Coffee, AL; Dale, AL; Geneva, AL; Henry, AL; Houston, AL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 9:11AM EDT until October 5 at 12:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Southern Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Northeastern Geneva County in southeastern Alabama...
Southwestern Henry County in southeastern Alabama...
Northwestern Houston County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 811 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daleville, Dothan, Fort Rucker, Headland, Hartford, Midland City,
Kinsey, Level Plains, Newton, Webb, Pinckard, Clayhatchee,
Grimes, Newville, Napier Field and Coffee Springs.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 5 at 2:46AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees.
This will yield at least major heat risk, impacting anyone without
adequate cooling and hydration.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, and
gusty winds will create erratic fire behavior for new or
existing fires.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In South Central MT Fire Zones...123...124.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central MT...Wheatland.
In South Central MT...Park...Sweet Grass.
In Southwest MT...Gallatin.

* WIND: West 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 12 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: up to 87 degrees.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS: The worst conditions are expected across
the lower to mid elevations in fine fuels.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute
to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued October 5 at 12:06AM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
104 to 107. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Watch means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, may occur. Actions should be taken to lessen
the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY EVENING

Glenn and Richardson Highways, especially from Glennallen west to

the Copper River Basin through Monday morning. With temperatures
around freezing for most locations, any precipitation may fall as

significant snow and ice accumulation is expected. However, the

freezing may result in slippery road conditions and patchy black
ice. The precipitation and fog is expected to taper off by early
to mid Monday morning.

511.alaska.gov.

evening tides of 6.5 to 7 ft are expected.

Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Most
susceptible areas will be Long Beach and Avalon Harbor Tuesday

Friday.

currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
morning and evening high tides, including over beach parking
lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion
is possible to likely.

into the weekend.
properties.instruction:

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 140 miles southwest of
Utirik. Scatterometry data indicates 15 to 20 kt winds near
Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap, with winds up to 25 kt
near heavier showers. TD 27W will be generally slow to move,
remaining over the northern Marshall Islands through Tuesday night.
Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms may lead to
locally heavy rainfall and flooding. Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of
rain with locally higher amounts are possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

27W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the Significant Tropical
Weather Advisory from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 4 at 3:39PM CDT until October 5 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 4 at 1:16PM PDT until October 7 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures of 94 to 102 degrees expected and low
temperatures in the mid 60s to low 70s, with widespread Moderate
HeatRisk and areas of Major HeatRisk.

* WHERE...Sacramento and northern San Joaquin Valleys, Delta and
Carquinez Strait, and foothills.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses, especially to
anyone without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Hottest days expected Monday through
Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Georgia where locally heavy rainfall since Friday afternoon has
primed the region more so than the rest of our area, so it wont
take as much rain to cause flash flooding. Across the flood watch
area, very high rain rates due to the tropical air mass may lead
to flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
